dimensions.assessment: Affects institutions of higher education, health professions students, disadvantaged student scholarship recipients, and public health workforce trainees nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: To reauthorize programs related to health professions education, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Continues funding streams for educational grants, loan repayments, and training programs across multiple health disciplines.
dimensions.evidence: appropriated $28,422,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes specific annual appropriations for multiple grant programs, such as $55,014,000 for scholarships for disadvantaged students and $49,924,000 for primary care training annually from FY 2026 through FY 2030.
dimensions.evidence: appropriated, $2,310,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

dimensions.assessment: Amends existing sections of the Public Health Service Act to extend authorization periods and funding amounts for established federal health education programs.
dimensions.evidence: Section 736(i) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 293(i)) is amended by striking... and inserting... for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

dimensions.assessment: Extends programs for a defined five-year period covering fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
dimensions.evidence: for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill reauthorizes numerous health professions education programs under the Public Health Service Act through fiscal years 2026 through 2030, maintaining specific funding levels for centers of excellence, disadvantaged student scholarships, training programs, and workforce analysis.
